title: The Gaussian propeller bound
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Gaussian propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor: for every finite measurable partition of a Euclidean space, the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian first moments of its cells is at most 9/(8 pi), with equality for three planar sectors of angle 2 pi/3. The course proves the duality with Gaussian maxima and the structure of optimal partitions; bounds the measure of a cell by half-space and spherical-cap rearrangement; deletes one score and uses Ehrhard's inequality for the gap probabilities; bounds residual covariance determinants against the cell with the shortest moment; and excludes five or more cells by a probability budget with exact rational margins. Consequences: a sharp inequality for expected maxima of Gaussian vectors, and the NP-hardness of improving the factor (8 pi/9)(1 - 1/k) for kernel clustering with the identity target. Named statements: the three-dimensional case (Heilman, Jagannath and Naor) and Ehrhard's inequality; for the hardness application also Khot and Naor's low-influence bound and the Unique Games theorem.
prerequisites: core course Measure and Integration (Fremlin, Measure Theory, Volumes 1 and 2): dominated convergence and differentiation under the integral sign (123C, 123D); Fubini's theorem (252B); linear changes of variable (263A); polar coordinates in the plane (263G); Hausdorff measure under Lipschitz maps (264G); integration over spheres and their surface area (265G, 265H)
Gaussian vectors: covariance, densities, independence of uncorrelated jointly Gaussian variables
for the last lesson: Unique Games instances and polynomial-time reductions

open_obligations: (HJN) S. Heilman, A. Jagannath and A. Naor, Solution of the propeller conjecture in R^3, arXiv:1112.2993, Theorem 1.1: for every finite measurable partition of R^3 the sum of the squared Gaussian first moments is at most 9/(8 pi); the proof is computer-assisted. Used in Theorem 4.3 of the first lesson (optimal partitions with at most four active cells), hence in Theorem 7.1 of the fifth lesson and in everything that uses it.

(EHR) Ehrhard's inequality for closed convex sets (A. Ehrhard, Mathematica Scandinavica 53 (1983); further proofs by van Handel, arXiv:1605.00285, and Neeman and Paouris, arXiv:1605.07233). Used in Lemma 3.1 of the third lesson (concavity of Phi^{-1} of the Gaussian measure of the translates of a convex cone), hence in Proposition 5.2 there, in Theorem 7.1 and in everything after.

(KN-INF) S. Khot and A. Naor, Approximate kernel clustering, arXiv:0807.4626, Theorem 3.8 (low-influence bound, via the invariance principle of Mossel, O'Donnell and Oleszkiewicz). Used only in Theorem 4.1 of the last lesson.
(UGT) OpenAI, The Unique Games Theorem (OpenAI Math Release preprint, 23 Sep 2026; family 102), Theorem 1.1. Used only in Theorem 4.1 of the last lesson.

(KN-ROUND) S. Khot and A. Naor, Theorem 2.1 of arXiv:0807.4626 (rounding with expected loss factor (8 pi/9)(1 - 1/k) for the identity target): quoted for context in the last lesson, not used in a proof.
